[1/5] Add a Play surface for browser games: auto-synced Prism-Relay build, a local-play card for Crypt-Crawler, version/commit display, dossier Play buttons and a cache-coherent shell

impact_assessment.why: The portfolio can show a game but cannot start it; visitors must clone a repository to try a playable project
impact_assessment.benefits: One click from a game dossier or the Play page starts Prism-Relay in the browser, shows its exact version and commit, and the weekly sync keeps it current without hand-copying files
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new Play page/manifest, Django? no; dependency: only standard library plus a weekly Actions checkout; concurrency: sync workflow versus site edits; state: versioned game directories and the shell cache
impact_assessment.mitigation: Version the copied build by commit, write a digest manifest, add a check mode and CI workflow, keep Crypt-Crawler as an explicit local-run card because its Python API cannot run on static Pages, and pin all new files in tests

[1/1] Remove Crypt-Crawler from the Play catalog; enforce the Prism-Relay static contract in --check-source and --write; record web-specific guidelines in Prism-Relay; 86 Python tests, 14 play, 88 project, 67 atlas and 58 verifier assertions; 4/4 gates; checklists: passed

impact_assessment.why: Crypt-Crawler needs its Python API and cannot run on static Pages, so advertising it as playable would be misleading; future Prism-Relay changes must be checked against the website's static contract
impact_assessment.benefits: The Play page lists only a build that actually runs; Prism-Relay developers get explicit rules, a PLAYABLE.md contract and an enforceable check-source gate before the website copies a build
impact_assessment.risks: contract: playable manifest/workflow now one game and a stricter source validator; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: copied Prism build unchanged
impact_assessment.mitigation: Run the source check, manifest check, full suites and gates; commit the Prism guidelines separately and keep the copied build's digest stable

[1/4] Add Weft to the versioned Play catalog: sync contract, manifest, logo, workflow checkout, parity tests and the noscript fallback

impact_assessment.why: The Play page can serve any static browser build, but the catalog still lists only Prism Relay. Weft is finished, static and zero-dependency, so it can become the second playable title without a new server or page.
impact_assessment.benefits: Visitors get a second one-click game; the sync validator now proves two independent builds against the same static contract; the weekly workflow keeps both versions, commits and digests current.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: tools/sync_playable_games.py, the manifest and the workflow; dependency: the Weft repository must be published for the CI checkout; concurrency: the sync workflow writes docs/play, the manifest and the pinned AGL license; state: commit-versioned build directories and a digest.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add one GAMES entry and one runtime tuple, validate the source against the existing static contract, generate the logo and manifest, update both parity suites, and keep the local build playable even before the repository is published.

[1/2] Restore previous Prism-Relay and Weft builds, retain three builds per game, bump the shell to v11 and version the catalog request

impact_assessment.why: A returning visitor's cached catalog still pointed at build directories the sync had deleted, so the Play iframe opened a 404 while a fresh browser worked.
impact_assessment.benefits: Cached catalogs resolve for the last two releases; the v11 shell and versioned manifest request bypass stale caches; the weekly sync keeps a bounded history.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: build retention and the shell version; dependency: none beyond GitHub Pages; concurrency: weekly sync, service-worker clients and a background Reforge pass; state: extra commit-named build directories.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Restore the two deleted builds, keep the current plus two predecessors, version the catalog query, run all Python and Node suites, then verify the old and current live paths.
